title: Certificates of Deposit: The Penalty Entry and Withdrawal Examined for a Grace-Period Charge
content:
For Certificates of Deposit held at Piedmont Crescent Bank, deciding whether a penalty was charged on money taken out in grace, the bank looks at one penalty entry and the withdrawal it was charged on. This page identifies both.

## The penalty entry

The penalty looked at is the most recently posted penalty entry on the certificate. Its booked sum and its posting date are taken from that entry alone.

A penalty that is no longer the most recent one on the certificate is not examined here; once a later penalty has posted, the earlier one falls under the general grounds for reversing penalties.

## The withdrawal it belongs to

Every penalty entry carries a reference to the ledger item that gave rise to it. The withdrawal examined is the withdrawal entry that this reference names. Where the proceeds of that withdrawal went, its destination and the receiving account, are read from that withdrawal entry.

## A penalty is credited back once at most

If the ledger already holds a reversal entry pointing to this penalty, the penalty has been dealt with and is not credited back a second time.

## Input, judgement, outcome (hypothetical ledger)

| Penalty entries on the certificate | Reversal pointing to the latest? | Entry examined |
|---|---|---|
| One, posted 22 September | No | That entry, and the withdrawal its reference names |
| Two, posted 4 March and 22 September | No | The 22 September entry only |
| One, posted 22 September | Yes | None; already credited back |
